primary: Page-aligned vs stock-matched offset in one external allocation at 256 KiB cap and offer.
method: All four arms in each cell/block share one live flat kqueue owner, eight established AF_UNIX streams, an identical compiled pump, two-worker 128-event budget, and the same producer and consumer storage. All tested buffers have an equal usable span of one cap. The matched arm uses the runtime modulo-page address of the real inline scratch. The offset128 arm starts 128 bytes after the backing page; the page arm starts at that page. All three share the same backing allocation. The embedded arm controls for scratch relocation. Each arm warms one wave after touching scratch, then produces, forwards and byte-verifies 64 MiB in fixed-size waves on a background thread. Owner CPU covers drains only. Wall throughput includes all three roles and validation. Both FINs and reverse traffic verified. ASan/UBSan qualification forces partial writes and verifies buffered tails for each arm at both caps. Each of sixteen blocks uses randomized cell order with balanced four-arm order. Intervals resample the median paired percentage change. No VM, IP, or concurrent consumer. The read and write both use the chosen address, so their effects cannot be separated.
